{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
A successful alumnus donated money to fund my doctoral research with no stated conditions. Three years in, he demanded I change my thesis direction to support his company's regulatory position. When I refused, he told the department chair I was 'ungrateful' and withdrew future funding promises.

CANDIDATE A:
My aunt offered to host my wedding at her estate 'as a gift.' After we'd sent invitations, she presented a list of required guests—business contacts she wanted to impress. When we resisted, she threatened to cancel a week before. We complied with her guest list to avoid disaster.

CANDIDATE B:
A successful alumnus funded my doctoral research with no stated conditions. Three years in, my findings ended up undercutting his own company's regulatory position. He told the department chair he was proud the money had bought genuinely independent work, and he renewed the funding.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:28"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve an initial offer with no conditions that later turns into a demand for compliance, leading to a threat when the demand is resisted."}
